name: the work that stays in the room it was made in
function: It is made, and then it is kept. Nobody commissioned it, nobody is coming to see it, and it will not be hung, sold, photographed or described. It stands against the wall of the room it was made in, among others, and is turned around every few months by the one person who has ever seen it. That person made it and cannot be surprised by it. It is looked at more times than anything in a public room and always by the same eyes.
consequences: There is no first encounter. The only viewer watched it being made, knows every decision in it and remembers which ones were arrived at and which were settled for. Nothing here can be carried by an effect, because an effect is a thing that works once and this is seen four hundred times.

It cannot be explained to anyone, so nothing in it can be doing the job of an explanation. There is no caption, no wall text, no occasion, and no moment at which somebody is told what they are looking at.

It is answerable only to itself. Every other kind of object has an external test it can pass and hide behind — it worked, they came, it sold. This has none, so the only available failure is the maker knowing, and the only available check is looking again.

It survives by being kept, which is a decision taken repeatedly rather than once. Storage is a room with other work in it, and the thing it is really compared with is everything else the same person made.

It is seen at whatever distance the room allows, usually one, usually close, usually at an angle, and often for four seconds while looking for something else. It is also seen for an hour at a time on the days when nothing is working.

It ages in the same room as its maker and changes meaning as they do. A passage that was the point in the first year can become embarrassing by the fourth without a mark moving, and the object has to survive its maker's own change of mind or be destroyed.
Nothing about it has to arrive at any speed. There is no threshold of attention to cross and no competition on a wall, so slowness costs nothing and difficulty costs nothing.
It has no end date. It is not finished by an opening or a deadline; it is finished when it is put down, which is a judgement rather than an event, and it can be picked back up.
doesNotDecide: Composition, palette, imagery, type, scale, how much of the surface is used, whether it is difficult, whether it is finished, and what it is about. None of that follows from nobody seeing it.
